title: Request Body with Pydantic
description: Receive and validate JSON request bodies using Pydantic models.

slides.title: Receiving JSON Data
slides.content:
# Declare a Request Body

In FastAPI, you can declare a parameter of a Pydantic model type. FastAPI will read the JSON body, validate it, and pass the model instance to your function.

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel

app = FastAPI()

class Item(BaseModel):
    name: str
    price: float

@app.post("/items/")
def create_item(item: Item):
    return {"item_name": item.name, "item_price": item.price}
```

- The request body must be JSON.
- Validation errors will return a 422 response automatically.

slides.title: Try it Yourself
slides.content: Send a POST request to `/items/` with JSON body.

quizData.question: How does FastAPI know to read a request body as a Pydantic model?

options.text: You must use a special decorator
By using a parameter of a Pydantic model type

quizData.explanation: When a function parameter is annotated with a Pydantic model, FastAPI automatically extracts the JSON body and validates it.

slides.title: Combining Path, Query, and Body
slides.content:
# Mixed Parameters

You can combine path, query, and body parameters in one endpoint.

```python
@app.put("/items/{item_id}")
def update_item(item_id: int, item: Item, q: str = None):
    return {"item_id": item_id, "item": item, "query": q}
```

- Path: `item_id`
- Query: `q`
- Body: `item` (Item model)

FastAPI intelligently distinguishes between them.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content: You can also use multiple body parameters by using `Body()` from FastAPI, but for most cases, a single Pydantic model is cleanest.
